sources.entry: InjectionIII - overdue Swift rewrite of Injection.

summary.one_liner: InjectionIII is a macOS app that enables Swift "hot reloading" by recompiling edited source files and injecting the new code into a running iOS, tvOS, or macOS app without a full rebuild or restart.
summary.what_it_does: The app watches for saved Swift source files, recompiles each changed file into a dynamic library by finding the swift-frontend invocation in recent Xcode build logs, and loads that library into the running app. It uses Apple's linker "interposing" (enabled via -Xlinker -interposable in Debug builds) to redirect calls to updated functions and methods, and also updates vtable dispatch for non-final class methods and handles legacy Objective-C swizzling. Developers add a short #if DEBUG snippet that loads a bundle from the app's Resources folder, and classes can implement an @objc injected() method to refresh the UI after injection. The README also covers SwiftUI support via @ObserveInjection and .enableInjection() from the HotSwiftUI or Inject packages, device injection using a copy_bundle.sh build phase script, an optional MCP server (v5.2.1+), and INJECTION_TRACE/INJECTION_DETAIL environment variables for debugging. Xcode 16.3 requires an EMIT_FRONTEND_COMMAND_LINES build setting to keep build-log parsing working.
use_cases: hot reload Swift code in iOS simulator
speed up UI tweaking during iOS development
inject code changes into running app on device
trace function calls with argument values during development
how_to_run: Download a release of InjectionIII.app from GitHub or the Mac App Store and launch it
Add #if DEBUG Bundle(path: "/Applications/InjectionIII.app/Contents/Resources/iOSInjection.bundle")?.load() (or tvOSInjection / macOSInjection bundle) to app startup code
Add -Xlinker and -interposable to Other Linker Flags for the Debug configuration only
Run the app in the simulator and save a Swift source file to see it report as injected
For Xcode 16.3+, add user-defined build setting EMIT_FRONTEND_COMMAND_LINES = YES to the Debug configuration
For devices, run: defaults write com.johnholdsworth.InjectionIII deviceUnlock any, then use the copy_bundle.sh build phase script
notable: Hot reloads Swift methods and computed properties in a running app without restarting it
Uses linker interposing rather than only swizzling, so it covers any Swift method
Reads Xcode build logs to learn how to recompile each changed file; Xcode 16.3 needs a build setting to keep this working
Supports SwiftUI injection through @ObserveInjection and .enableInjection() from HotSwiftUI or Inject
Includes an INJECTION_TRACE mode that logs calls to injected functions with their argument values
caveats: Cannot inject changes to stored property layout, and adding or removing methods on non-final classes is not supported
On macOS and device use, the app sandbox and hardened runtime library validation must be turned off during development; the App Store version is sandboxed and works differently
Adding, renaming, or deleting source files during injection can break it; a rebuild or relaunch may be needed
The README calls InjectionNext a successor and suggests trying it if InjectionIII's limits are hit
